title: Roles: executive, CPO, senior supplier and project assurance
blurb: Apply the guidance for the four governance-level roles: who does what, and which person in a people list best fits each role.
question: At Saltmarsh Housing Group, which person in the people list is best suited to the chief product owner role for Repairs Reimagined, and why?

teach.body: Four of the 11 PRINCE2 Agile roles work above day-to-day management. The project executive is accountable for the project and its strategic alignment. The chief product owner (CPO) represents the user community and owns the project backlog. The senior supplier represents the supplier side. Project assurance monitors, independently of the project manager, whether the project follows PRINCE2 Agile principles and agile practices.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 7.2, Table B.1

teach.h: What each role does, and the clue in a people list
head: Role
Key duties
People-list clue
rows: Accountable; approves brief, approaches, team structure and agile tolerances; role model
Received the mandate; holds the budget
Represents users; owns project backlog; priorities across teams
Knows users' needs; sets direction for the product
Represents the supplier side; commits its people and resources
Commits supplier staff; owns the contract on that side
Monitors adherence; quality and governance checks; advises board
Independent; reports to the board or audit

teach.caption: In starting up, the executive leads the project canvas; the PM creates the project backlog in consultation with the CPO, senior supplier and executive (Table 13.1).

teach.h: Project assurance and its near misses
How to choose a person for a role
teach.body: Read each background for what the person does now and whose interests they hold. Holding the budget or receiving the mandate points to the executive. Speaking for users, or setting direction for a user-facing product, points to the CPO. Committing a supplier's staff points to the senior supplier. Independence from delivery and reporting to the board points to project assurance. A respected but sceptical user is usually a key influencer, not the CPO.

Operations director Graham Doyle received the mandate and holds the capital budget: project executive. Head of maintenance Ruth Kenyon leads the engineers who will use and own the dashboard: CPO. Dev Patel commits Senticore's fitting teams and owns its contract: senior supplier. Quality director Robert Kale is independent of operations and reports to the board: project assurance. Stuart Bell, respected and sceptical, is a key influencer, and Leanne Park, who runs the team backlog, fits a product owner role.

teach.text: Classic swaps: the CPO prioritizes across teams and owns the project backlog, while a PO owns one team's backlog. The executive approves tolerances for agile decision-making, not the CPO. Project assurance monitors and advises; project support does the administration and dashboards.

items: Executive: accountable; approves brief, approaches, structure and agile tolerances; role model.
CPO: represents users; owns and refines the project backlog; priorities across teams.
Senior supplier: represents the supplier side and commits its people and resources.
Project assurance: independent; monitors adherence; advises on issues, risks, exceptions and canvas.
Match people by whose interests they hold and what they control now.

summary: You can now apply the guidance for the project executive, CPO, senior supplier and project assurance. You can also pick the best person for each role from a people list and spot the classic near-miss roles.

A.q: Saltmarsh Housing Group needs a chief product owner for Repairs Reimagined, which has two delivery teams. Which person is best suited to the role?
options: Raj Malhotra, who prioritizes the service design team's work
Deborah Kiely, head of tenant engagement, who knows tenants' needs
Winston Clarke, chair of the tenants' panel for twenty years
Margaret Oyelaran, chief executive, who received the mandate
A.why: The CPO represents the user community, owns the project backlog and sets priorities across teams (Table 7.2). Deborah works closely with tenants and understands their needs across the whole service.

whyNot.0: Prioritizing one team's work fits a product owner, who does not prioritize across teams.
whyNot.2: The panel chair is a strong key influencer and user voice, but he is not placed to own the project backlog across teams.
whyNot.3: The chief executive received the mandate and is accountable: the project executive.

A.q: At Pinewick Home and Garden, the teams want to know how far they may adjust store roll-out order and features without referring upwards. Which role should approve the tolerances for this agile decision-making?
options: Project executive
Chief product owner
Senior supplier
Project assurance
A.why: The project executive approves tolerances for agile decision-making (Table B.1, Table 7.2).

whyNot.1: The CPO sets priorities across teams within the tolerances; it does not approve them.
whyNot.2: The senior supplier represents the supplier side; it does not approve agile tolerances.
whyNot.3: Assurance monitors and advises; it does not approve tolerances.

A.q: Callowmere University wants someone to provide project assurance for the Student Support Hub. Which person is best suited to the role?
options: Jamal Hussain, project manager from the change office
Chloe Hartley, Scrum master for the web team
Sinead Walsh, independent quality and enhancement manager
Rebecca Lyle, who manages the web team's backlog
A.why: Project assurance monitors adherence to PRINCE2 Agile principles and agile practices and builds quality and governance checks into delivery, independently of the PM (Table 7.2). Sinead reviews services against standards and is independent of the wellbeing service.

whyNot.0: Assurance must be independent of the project manager; Jamal is the PM.
whyNot.1: A Scrum master fits the team coach role.
whyNot.3: Managing a team backlog fits the product owner role.

B.q: Larkspur Rail's people list describes Gemma Lowther as account director at Coinbridge Payments, who commits Coinbridge's staff and owns the contract on the supplier side. Which role does she best fit?
options: Chief product owner
Project assurance
Product owner
Senior supplier
B.why: The senior supplier represents the supplier side: those who design, develop and deliver the products, committing the supplier's people and resources.

whyNot.0: The CPO represents the users, not the supplier.
whyNot.1: Assurance must be independent; a supplier account director is not independent of delivery.
whyNot.2: A product owner leads one delivery team's backlog day to day; Gemma's role is at the supplier's senior level.

B.q: Senticore warns that sensor fitting at Draycott will overrun, and the project manager prepares an exception report. The board wants independent advice on how this affects the project canvas. Which role should provide it?
options: Project assurance
Project support
Agile coach
Chief product owner
B.why: Project assurance advises the board and PM on assessing and resolving issues, risks and exception reports, and checks for impacts against the project canvas (Table B.1).

whyNot.1: Project support provides administration and dashboard updates, not independent advice.
whyNot.2: The agile coach advises on agile adoption and practices, not on exception impacts.
whyNot.3: The CPO represents users and priorities; the independent advice is assurance's.

B.q: In starting up at Callowmere, the project manager is defining what the project will deliver and creating the project backlog with its epics. Which roles should he consult?
options: The team coach, product owner and developers
The CPO, the senior supplier and the executive
Project support and project assurance together
The agile coach and the data protection officer
B.why: In 'prepare the outline business case', the PM, in consultation with the CPO, senior supplier and project executive, defines what is to be delivered and creates the project backlog (Table 13.1).

whyNot.0: Team-level roles refine product backlogs later; the project backlog is shaped with the governance roles.
whyNot.2: Support helps with administration and assurance monitors; neither is the named consultee here.
whyNot.3: Specialists may advise, but the consultation named in the book is with the CPO, senior supplier and executive.

C.q: Pinewick's retail operations director appoints Anita Shah, the e-commerce product manager who manages the e-commerce team's backlog, as chief product owner for both delivery teams. Head of e-commerce Marcus Lindell represents online customers' needs. Is this appointment appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because she already manages a team's backlog
Yes, because the CPO is a version of the team manager
No, because her experience fits a team-level product owner
No, because the CPO must come from outside the business
C.why: The CPO represents the user community and sets priorities across teams; a person who manages one team's backlog fits the product owner role, which owns one team's product backlog (Table 7.2). Marcus is the better CPO fit.

whyNot.0: Managing one team's backlog is the PO's job; it is not the cross-team user representation a CPO needs.
whyNot.1: The product owner, not the CPO, is the version of the team manager role (7.3.1).
whyNot.3: There is no such rule; the CPO represents users and is typically from the business.

C.q: Draycott's board asks Robert Kale, the quality director who is independent of operations and reports to the board, to provide project assurance and check that quality and governance checks are built into each iteration. Is this appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because assurance compiles reports from the dashboards
Yes, because assurance is independent monitoring of the project
No, because the project manager should assure the project
No, because quality checks are a task for the testers
C.why: Project assurance monitors adherence to PRINCE2 Agile principles and agile practices, integrates quality and governance checks into iterative delivery and must be independent of the PM; Robert fits (Table 7.2).

whyNot.0: Compiling reports from dashboards is project support's work.
whyNot.2: Assurance must be independent of the project manager.
whyNot.3: Testers check products against criteria and the DoD; governance checks across iterations are assurance's.

C.q: Larkspur's commercial director, Bronwen Hale, is project executive. She approves the tolerances within which the teams flex scope and, to model agile working, reviews the project dashboard instead of asking for a long written report. Is this appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because the executive approves tolerances and models agile
Yes, because the executive owns and refines the project backlog
No, because project assurance approves the agile tolerances
No, because the board should receive written monthly reports
C.why: The project executive approves tolerances for agile decision-making and is a role model for agile adoption (Table B.1). Pulling information from the project dashboard fits agile progress control.

whyNot.1: The CPO owns and refines the project backlog.
whyNot.2: Assurance monitors and advises; the executive approves tolerances.
whyNot.3: In agile the project dashboard replaces the highlight report, and the board pulls information from it (Table 12.1).

reteach.title: Who sits around the table?
reteach.question: Picture the people steering a new community sports centre. Who plays each governance role?

blocks.body: The council director who holds the budget and answers for success is the project executive. The head of community sport, who speaks for the clubs and residents and decides which facilities come first, is the CPO. The builder's director, who commits the construction crews, is the senior supplier. The council's independent auditor, who checks the project is run as agreed, provides project assurance.

blocks.text: The loudest user, or the person who runs one team's backlog, is not automatically the CPO. Look for the person who represents all users across teams.

explain.body: Accountable for the project and its strategic alignment. Approves the project brief, management approaches and team structure, and the tolerances for agile decision-making. Leads the project canvas in starting up and models agile adoption.
explain.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table B.1, Table 13.1

test.q: At Easterholm County Council, Sarah Pennington, director of adult social services, received the mandate for Care Online and is accountable for the grant. Which role does she best fit?
options: Chief product owner
Senior supplier
Project executive
Project assurance
test.why: The person who received the mandate and is accountable for the funding fits the project executive, who is accountable for the project (Table 7.2).

whyNot.0: The CPO represents users and owns the project backlog.
whyNot.1: The senior supplier represents the supplier side.
whyNot.3: Assurance is independent monitoring, not accountability for the project.

explain.body: Represents the user community; owns the project backlog and keeps it refined with user input and aligned with the team product backlogs; makes sure priorities are clear across teams and user requirements are met.

test.q: Which person at Draycott Precision Engineering is best suited to the chief product owner role?
options: Leanne Park, who manages the software team's backlog
Stuart Bell, a respected senior engineer who doubts prediction
Graham Doyle, operations director holding the budget
Ruth Kenyon, head of maintenance who will own the dashboard
test.why: Ruth leads the engineers who will use the dashboard and will own it afterwards, so she represents the users across the project (Table 7.2).

whyNot.0: Managing one team's backlog fits the product owner.
whyNot.1: A respected sceptic is a key influencer for adoption, not the backlog owner.
whyNot.2: The budget holder who received the mandate is the project executive.

explain.body: Represents those who design, develop and deliver the products and commits the supplier's people and resources. Consulted when the project backlog is created.
explain.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.1; PRINCE2 7 role

test.q: Which person at Saltmarsh Housing Group best fits the senior supplier role for the repairs work?
options: Ian Thursby, repairs director managing the Coastline contract
Kyle Morgan, an informal leader in the contact centre
Ellen Price, who configures the tenant portal
Frank Tolley, who commits Coastline's engineers
test.why: Frank commits Coastline's engineers and owns the contract on Coastline's side, so he represents the supplier.

whyNot.0: Ian manages the contract for the customer side, not the supplier.
whyNot.1: Kyle is a key influencer among contact centre staff.
whyNot.2: Ellen does delivery work in the digital team, a team-level role.

explain.body: Monitors adherence to PRINCE2 Agile principles and agile practices; builds quality and governance checks into iterative delivery; gives feedback that balances agility with control; advises the board and PM on issues, risks, exception reports and canvas impacts. Independent of the PM.
explain.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 7.2, Table B.1

test.q: Which person at Saltmarsh Housing Group is best suited to project assurance?
options: Sally Greaves, the project manager, new to the association
Amara Okeke, analyst who measures tenant satisfaction
Dr Laura Benn, who reports to the audit and risk committee
Joy Ansah, contact centre manager leading 28 advisers
test.why: Laura is head of governance and assurance and reports to the board's audit and risk committee, giving the independence assurance needs (Table 7.2).

whyNot.0: Assurance must be independent of the project manager.
whyNot.1: An analyst who measures service performance fits the tester role better.
whyNot.3: Joy manages a team affected by the change; she is not independent.
